scenarios.purpose: A complete-looking header declares a ten-byte payload while only five payload bytes are supplied, so the decoder's own header/payload arithmetic must detect the shortfall.
A sixteen-bit-form header declares a thousand-byte payload against a two-hundred-byte configured cap, and no payload byte is ever supplied.
Three emitted binary frames at payload lengths 5, 125 and 126 expose which length form the encoder chose, through the exact wire size of each frame.
A received close frame carries status code 1006, which RFC 6455 forbids on the wire.
A received close frame carries status code 1000, which must be admitted and echoed.
A received close frame carries valid status code 1000 with a reason that is not valid UTF-8, which validation must reject as a typed protocol fault.
A non-final text fragment carrying "he" is followed by a final continuation carrying "llo", so an in-order assembly delivers exactly "hello".
A non-final continuation frame arrives with no started fragment sequence, which admission control must reject.
A ping frame arrives with the FIN bit clear, which control-frame validation must reject.
A ping frame declares an extended payload length, which exceeds the 125-octet control bound.

bindings.chain_rationale: The header and payload arithmetic, and the packet-size comparison it feeds, are both inside translateSingleFrame itself.

clauses.statement: A frame header that declares more payload than the buffer holds is detected by the decoder's own header/payload arithmetic, and nothing is allocated or delivered for it.

mutation.expectation: Dropping the payload term from the real packet size makes the arithmetic believe a two-byte header is the whole frame, so the shortfall is no longer detected.

bindings.chain_rationale: translateSingleFrame delegates the configured-cap comparison to translateSingleFrameCheckLengthLimit, a private helper in the same compilation unit, and calls it before the payload buffer is allocated.

clauses.statement: A frame declaring a payload above the configured cap is rejected as a typed too-big fault while only its four header bytes have been supplied, so no payload byte is ever retained.

mutation.expectation: With the configured-cap comparison disabled the oversized declaration is accepted and the frame merely waits for payload bytes that never arrive.

bindings.chain_rationale: createBinaryFrame delegates octet emission to createByteBufferFromFramedata, which asks getSizeBytes which length form to use. All three are private or public members of the same compilation unit.

clauses.statement: Emitted frames whose payload length is at most 125 use the seven-bit form, so their wire size is exactly the payload plus a two-byte header.

mutation.expectation: With the seven-bit form never selected, a five-byte payload is emitted with a four-byte header instead of a two-byte one.

clauses.statement: The seven-bit form stops exactly at 125: a 126-byte payload is emitted with the extended sixteen-bit form, so its wire size is the payload plus a four-byte header.

mutation.expectation: Moving the boundary one byte out makes a 126-byte payload take the seven-bit form, changing its wire size from 130 to 128.

bindings.chain_rationale: CloseFrame.isValid is called on every decoded close frame and holds the status-code and reason checks.

clauses.statement: A received close frame carrying a status code that must not appear on the wire is rejected as a typed protocol fault.

mutation.expectation: With the unsendable-code test disabled, status code 1006 is admitted instead of rejected.

clauses.statement: A received close frame carrying a valid status code is admitted, closes the connection with that code, and is echoed.

mutation.expectation: Widening the illegal-code test to every code turns the admitted 1000 close into a rejection, so validation cannot be vacuously permissive.

clauses.statement: A received close frame whose reason is not valid UTF-8 is rejected as a typed protocol fault carrying close code 1007.

mutation.expectation: Skipping the reason test should change the outcome for a close frame whose reason is not valid UTF-8.

bindings.chain_rationale: Both fragment admission and the hand-off that completes an assembled message are decided inside this member.

clauses.statement: A non-final text fragment followed by a final continuation is assembled, in order, into exactly one delivered message.

mutation.expectation: With the final-fragment test disabled the sequence is never completed, so the assembled message is never delivered.

clauses.statement: A continuation fragment that arrives with no started sequence is rejected as a typed protocol fault, so continuations are admitted only inside a sequence.

mutation.expectation: With the started-sequence test disabled an orphan continuation is silently admitted instead of rejected.

bindings.chain_rationale: ControlFrame.isValid is called on every decoded control frame. It holds the finality test; it does NOT hold the 125-octet length bound, which is why the second clause of this obligation carries no canary.

clauses.statement: A control frame that arrives with the FIN bit clear is rejected as a typed protocol fault.

mutation.expectation: With the finality test disabled a non-final control frame is no longer rejected here.

clauses.statement: A control frame declaring a payload length above 125 is rejected as a typed protocol fault.
clauses.no_canary_reason: The 125-octet control bound is not implemented in ControlFrame.isValid, which is the symbol the immutable catalog declares for this obligation. In the pinned source the bound is enforced in Draft_6455.translateSingleFramePayloadLength, a different compilation unit, so no edit inside this binding's chain can flip this clause's witnesses. The witnesses are recorded because the pinned Java does reject the frame; the clause is nonetheless unsatisfied because the rejection cannot be attributed to the bound construct.

unbound.detail: The catalog declares this obligation against Draft_6455.translateSingleFrame, the receive path. Java-WebSocket 1.6.0 accepts non-minimal sixteen-bit length encodings on receive, so the pinned construct does not implement canonicality and no honest witness exists at that symbol. The emit-side choice lives in createByteBufferFromFramedata, which is not the declared symbol for this obligation.

Same receive-path symbol as the sixteen-bit obligation, with the same non-minimal acceptance. The high-bit case additionally never reaches the pinned construct through this adapter: the java-oracle wire tracker rejects a sixty-four-bit header with the high bit set before Java decodes it, so any observation there would be an observation of the adapter, not of Draft_6455.

The immutable catalog declares this masking obligation against org.java_websocket.util.Charsetfunctions.utf8Bytes(Ljava/lang/String;)[B, which converts a string to UTF-8 bytes and has nothing to do with the RFC 6455 masking transform. Binding a masking witness to that symbol would be a false attribution, and the catalog cannot be edited, so this obligation stays unbound.
Declared against the same Charsetfunctions.utf8Bytes symbol as obligation.mask-equation, with the same mismatch.

Java-WebSocket 1.6.0's Draft_6455.translateSingleFrame reads the mask bit and unmasks when it is set, but performs no endpoint-role check on inbound masking: a server accepts an unmasked client frame. The declared construct therefore does not implement the obligation. Recorded as a Java-versus-RFC divergence in drafts/ledger-proposals/java-formal-binding-findings.json.

WebSocketImpl.decode is resolvable and on the executed path, and chunk-boundary invariance is observable, but this round found no edit inside decode that flips an invariance witness without breaking decoding outright, which would be a non-specific canary. Deferred rather than credited.
WebSocketImpl.closeConnection is resolvable and on the executed path; the absorbing-terminal-state clauses and their canaries were not built this round.

The java-oracle adapter executes one ordered scenario in a single thread and owns no executors, so it cannot exhibit concurrent command submission. Serialized-owner-order claims are not observable through it at any strength.

The catalog declares this obligation against WebSocketAdapter.onWebsocketPing, whose body sends the automatic pong. The java-oracle listener extends WebSocketAdapter and overrides onWebsocketPing without calling super, so the declared construct never executes under this adapter and no observation could be attributed to it.

The catalog declares this obligation against the exception type org.java_websocket.exceptions.InvalidDataException. The type declaration carries a close code and a constructor; the decisions that make faults typed and fail closed live at the throw sites in Draft_6455 and the framing classes, outside the declared symbol.

Declared against Draft_6455.translateSingleFrame, which this round already binds for two other obligations. A separate clause set and separate canaries are needed so that one witness cannot be credited to three obligations; that work was not done this round.

Declared against Draft_6455.createBinaryFrame. The role rules are observable, but the adapter deliberately omits client mask keys from its output because Java-WebSocket randomises them, so the XOR transform clause of this obligation cannot be witnessed. A binding on the role rules alone would be partial, and this round did not build it.

Declared against WebSocketImpl.startHandshake. The handshake oracle's client_request direction feeds raw client request bytes into the server-side translateHandshake path; it never runs startHandshake, so no observation could be attributed to the declared construct.

Declared against Draft_6455.postProcessHandshakeResponseAsServer, which the handshake oracle protocol does execute and whose Sec-WebSocket-Accept output it reads back. Binding it needs the separate java-websocket-handshake-oracle request shape, which this round's runner does not yet emit.

Declared against Draft_6455.translateSingleFrame. Its only witness available this round is the configured-cap rejection already credited to obligation.preallocation-cap, and crediting one witness to two obligations would inflate the numerator. A distinct clause targeting checkAlloc is needed, and checkAlloc is declared in Draft, a different compilation unit.

Declared against WebSocketListener.onWebsocketMessage(WebSocket, ByteBuffer). WebSocketListener is an interface: the declaration has no body, so it can host no canary. It is also one of two members named onWebsocketMessage, so the binding key declaringType#name is ambiguous and resolution is refused.
Declared against WebSocketListener.onWebsocketMessage(WebSocket, String), with the same body-less interface declaration and the same name ambiguity as the binary overload.

Declared against the type org.java_websocket.server.WebSocketServer. The java-oracle adapter deliberately owns no sockets and never instantiates a server, so the declared opening seam is not exercised.
